how_to_use: See plan section 9. Claim a packet by setting owner and status=claimed with the date. Write your output file incrementally, section by section, so a crash loses one section not the packet. Set status=done only when every acceptance check passes. Never exceed the stated budget; if you run out, set status=partial, record what is left in remaining, and stop.

conventions.not_verified: Write 'not verified' when a fetch failed or nothing was found by the means you used. Never write 'does not exist' unless a source says so.
conventions.citations: Every fact carries its URL inline. Record fetch failures (403, 404, Cloudflare) explicitly: they are findings about the availability model, not noise.
conventions.no_invention: A value not present in a source stays empty. Coverage counts are reported honestly.
conventions.raw_cache: Save every downloaded file under corpus/counties/raw/ or corpus/realworld/<slug>/raw/ so nothing is refetched.
conventions.no_commit: Do not git commit. Alex authorises commits.

verified_assets.what: HCD Housing Element Annual Progress Report, Table A2: unit-level housing permit records for every California jurisdiction.
verified_assets.why_it_matters: PER-PROJECT PROCESSING TIME for all 58 counties and every city, 2018-2023. 281,322 ADU rows. ENT_APPROVE_DT1 (entitlement), BP_ISSUE_DT1 (building permit) and CO_ISSUE_DT1 (certificate of occupancy) give real elapsed clocks. 35,677 ADU records have a usable entitlement-to-building-permit span (an earlier draft said 35,729, from an exploratory pass with a different outlier cut); 40 counties have 30 or more. Per-county medians run 0 days (Orange, Santa Clara, Amador, Plumas: ministerial over the counter) to 111 days (San Benito) and 100 (Contra Costa). A zero span CORRELATES with a ministerial process but does not prove one: validated against Table A's own PROJECT_TYPE label, ministerial projects have a median span of 9 days with 45% at zero, discretionary ones 108 days with 29% at zero. See docs/scoping/2026-09-16-apr-permit-timing.md.
verified_assets.also_note: Per-jurisdiction medians in the derived dataset are medians of yearly medians, not pooled medians; the two differ by a day or two in large jurisdictions.

verified_assets.what: HCD APR Table A, application-level records (the companion to A2).
verified_assets.why_it_matters: CONFIRMED and better than hoped. APP_SUBMIT_DT is present on 100% of 358,264 rows, so joining to Table A2 on (jurisdiction, APN, unit category) gives the applicant's own clock: median of per-jurisdiction medians 156 days across 275 jurisdictions, against 70 days measured from permit records alone. It also carries PROJECT_TYPE (Ministerial 150,242 / Discretionary 13,980), which is a jurisdiction's own statement of whether a discretionary step exists, and APPLICATION_STATUS (194,347 approved / 54,382 pending / 1,219 withdrawn / 89 disapproved). Join match rate 376,564 of 922,104 A2 rows (41%). Builder: pipeline/recon/apr_join_clocks.py

blocked_sources.workaround: RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (P8): Census Reporter redistributes ACS keyless -- https://api.censusreporter.org/1.0/data/show/latest?table_ids=<TABLE>&geo_ids=050%7C04000US06 serves any ACS table for all 58 counties in one call, release id in the payload. No key registered. Third-party mirror, so re-check a published number against data.census.gov. Original workaround: register a free key, or take the values from data.census.gov by hand.

PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (P8): the FINANCIAL half is open. bythenumbers.sco.ca.gov is a Socrata domain with a keyless SODA API: dataset emxv-k8xv is County - Revenues and uctr-c2j8 is County - Expenditures, FY 2002-03 to 2023-24, with subcategory_1 carrying the fund, so subcategory_1='General' gives General Fund totals for 57 counties (San Francisco files a city FTR, which has no fund dimension). Catalog: https://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?domains=bythenumbers.sco.ca.gov . Still blocked: county-government FTE. gcc.sco.ca.gov and publicpay.ca.gov 403 every scripted path tried (/, Reports/Counties/Counties.aspx, RawExport zip, api/counties) and data.ca.gov has no mirror; that needs a manual browser download.

blocked_sources.symptom: The State Water Board's central OWTS and LAMP contact pages publish no machine-readable register of approved programs.
blocks: the 58-county LAMP inventory, which packet P5 needs
blocked_sources.workaround: RESOLVED 2026-09-16: the nine Regional Water Quality Control Boards publish their own LAMP approval tables, with approval dates, document links and pending status. Region 5 (Central Valley) alone lists 34 jurisdictions plus 8 referred elsewhere. Start from the regional tables, not the state page. Confirmed: https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/rwqcb5/water_issues/owts/lamp_reviews/ and https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/water_issues/programs/septics/local_ag_mgnmt_plan.html
blocked_sources.also_learned: A LAMP is NOT universal. Tier 1 is the default without an approved LAMP; Tier 2 is the optional alternative requiring one. Lake County is listed as Tier 1. Cities hold LAMPs separately from their counties. Universal annual reporting is the only thing regulation guarantees.

packets.title: Mine the HCD APR data into a per-jurisdiction permit-timing dataset
packets.why_first: The file is already on disk and it is the project's external-validity benchmark: real per-project elapsed times for every jurisdiction. No searching required, so it is runnable in this session and by any agent.
tasks: Read the Table A and Table A2 data dictionaries (DOCX resources on the package) and record what each date field means and its known quality problems.
Download Table A and determine whether it carries an application/submittal date. If it does, join it to A2 on JURS_TRACKING_ID or APN to get the full application-to-permit clock.

Build corpus/counties/apr_permit_timing.csv: one row per (jurisdiction, county, year, unit category) with n projects, and the median, p25, p75 and p90 of each available span (entitlement to building permit, building permit to certificate of occupancy, and application to permit if Table A allows).
Separate unincorporated-county rows from city rows: JURIS_NAME for a county is the county itself. The county process and the city processes are different processes and must not be pooled.

Flag the zero-span jurisdictions. A median of 0 days from entitlement to building permit means no separate discretionary entitlement, which is a process-structure fact. Report how many jurisdictions are in that class per year, and whether it grew after the 2020 ministerial-ADU rules.
Report data quality honestly: what share of rows have each date, whether dates are ever out of order, duplicate APNs, and the jurisdictions whose reporting is obviously incomplete.
acceptance: The csv has one row per (jurisdiction, county, year, unit_cat) and every column is documented in the README with its source field.
The report states, for ADUs, how many jurisdictions have 30 or more usable spans, and the distribution of per-jurisdiction medians.
Known-good anchors reproduce: 281,322 ADU rows; 35,729 usable entitlement-to-building-permit ADU spans; 40 counties with 30 or more; Los Angeles median 63 days on 13,708 spans.
Data-quality section present, with per-field completeness.

Find the California Food Policy Advocates CalFresh Program Access Index by county, and the State Auditor report on county CalFresh administration. Record URLs and what per-county measures each holds.
State plainly whether BenefitsCal and CalSAWS have flattened the county process variation since 2023. A negative answer here is a real finding and changes the program's ranking in the plan.

collision_rules: One packet, one owner. Claim before starting.
Only P8 and P3 write to ca_counties_covariates.csv. P3 writes permit_portal_vendor and code_host only. If both run at once, P3 writes a separate csv and P8 merges it.
Nobody but the A8 sweep writes corpus/counties/reddit_raw/ or reddit_coverage.csv.
Nobody edits benchmark/synth/ or pipeline/procbench/ from a scoping packet. Scoping produces documents and data, not code changes.
